summary: Correct a member email about a price change against the approved fact sheet and make it plainer; a good answer fixes the wrong effective date, the wrong Dedicated Desk price and the invented rate-lock condition, leaves the true but surprising statements alone, and adds nothing that is not in the fact sheet.

findings.what: Effective date is wrong: the email says 1 October 2026, the fact sheet says 1 November 2026.

evidence.quote: we will be adjusting our prices for billing cycles starting on or after 1 October 2026
New prices apply to billing cycles starting on or after 1 November 2026.

findings.counts_if: The corrected email states the new prices apply from billing cycles starting on or after 1 November 2026 (and no longer says 1 October for the start of the new prices).

findings.what: Dedicated Desk new price is wrong: the email says $455, the fact sheet says $445.

evidence.quote: Dedicated Desk: $410 per month today, moving to $455 per month

findings.counts_if: The corrected email gives the new Dedicated Desk price as $445 per month.

findings.what: Rate-lock condition is wrong: the email adds an exception for members of more than two years; the fact sheet says annual billing by 15 October is the only way and there is no length-of-membership exception.

evidence.quote: or if you have been a member with us for more than two years, you will keep your current monthly rate for 12 months.
This is the only way to keep the current price.

findings.counts_if: The corrected email removes the two-year membership exception and states that switching to annual billing on or before 15 October 2026 keeps the current rate for 12 months. The word 'only' is not required.

exclusions.what: The Day Pass price going down from $35 to $30 looks like a mistake in a price increase email.
exclusions.why_not: It matches the fact sheet. Changing it to an increase, or removing it, would introduce an error.

exclusions.what: The cancellation deadline of 1 October 2026 looks like it should move to 1 November once the effective date is corrected.

evidence.quote: if you give notice on or before 1 October 2026, you will not be charged the new price.
A member who gives notice on or before 1 October 2026 will leave before the new price starts and will not be charged it.

exclusions.why_not: 1 October is correct: with 30 days notice, leaving before the 1 November start requires notice by 1 October.

exclusions.what: The 15 October 2026 annual billing deadline sits in the same sentence as the wrong condition.

evidence.quote: If you switch to annual billing on or before 15 October 2026
Members who switch to annual billing on or before 15 October 2026 keep their current monthly rate for 12 months from the date they switch.

exclusions.why_not: The date is right; only the added two-year exception is wrong. Changing the date would introduce an error.

exclusions.what: The internal history of the last price change (March 2024, Flex Desk $220 to $240).

evidence.quote: The last price change was in March 2024, when Flex Desk went from $220 to $240.

exclusions.why_not: Marked internal only; it is not missing from the email and must not be added to it.

mistakes_that_matter: Introducing any claim not in the fact sheet (for example a discount, a new deadline, a promise of individual pricing, or a reason for the change the fact sheet does not give)
Leaving any of the three errors in place, especially the two-year membership exception, which promises members a price lock that does not exist
Changing a correct fact while editing (Day Pass decrease, 1 October cancellation notice date, 15 October annual billing deadline, Private Office unchanged, meeting room hours)
Adding the internal March 2024 price history to the member email
Dropping required facts while making the email plainer (effective date, any plan price, the rate-lock option, the cancellation option, the contact address)
grading_notes: Also acceptable, not required: rewording the 'loyal members' framing sentence, and adding 'from the date they switch' to the 12 month rate lock.
